card.title: 74th SILESIAN REGIMENT
card.text: When an enemy unit moves into the frontline, pin it.
card.flavorText: The 74th Upper Silesian Infantry Regiment was a unit of the 7th Infantry Division of the Polish Army. In 1939 the division was attached to the Kraków Army which defended the southwest corner of Poland during the German invasion. The division was involved in heavy fighting before being forced to retreat and take up defenses near the town of Lelów. There the division was encircled by the German forces, and although elements of the 74th Regiment along with some cavalry and sappers managed to break out of the encirclement, the division surrendered as it had suffered such heavy casualties that it was no longer capable of fighting. During Operation Tempest (1944-1945), a series of uprising by the Polish Home Army against the German occupation, the 7th Infantry Division was recreated with the 74th and 27th Regiment. The division took part in heavy fighting against the Germans, but most men ceased fighting after central Poland had been taken over by the Soviets. Many of the men went back underground as they feared being arrested the Soviet NKVD due to their anti-Soviet and anti-communist sentiments.
